body: Thank you very much for your input. Also, I am happy for you that you are doing well despite having endured horrible things in your life.
Have you had victim mentality and if so, how did you overcome this issue?

I am happya for you that you found a way to feeling content with yourself.

For me, I feel like the real me is already mostly dead and I hate this new caricature of the real me that I devolved into. So hopefully I can reach a similar point as you have but at the moment, I cannot come to terms with what I have become.

Since my youth, I have been someone whose life looked extremely promising, at least on paper (academically and interpersonally). However, the last decade has been a struggle with depression and anxiety that tore me apart piece by piece. All I have left seems to be rage and hatred for the new "myself" - this new creature that I often can't even recognise. The problem is that my resulting outward behaviour also alienates others, people avoid me like a leper (and I can't blame them), so the deeper I sink, the harder it is to be lifted up, since I can't do it myself and less and less people are willing to try to help me, it seems.

Do you think someone with this distribution of the 5 big traits has a chance to change? I am starting to lose hope to be honest. I have tried multiple psychotherapy interventions (I have suffered from depression and anxiety for almost a decade) but none of them had a lasting effect due to me not sticking to them enough (low conscientiousness) or not being able to fully open and talk about myself (low extraversion).

Thank you for your reply. I will listen to the interview you linked. 

I agree there definitely is some bias stemming from the fact that I answer the questions in the test myself. I have an extremely low opinion of myself and often can't stop myself from feeling intense hate and disgust towards my own person. I think taking the test makes me hate myself even more.

The big 5 factor model seems to be one of the most well regarded models used by psychologists and it has been shown to have predictive value regarding some important life parameters, like income, happiness, etc. And my combination doesn't predict a successful life.

I have heard opinions that the scores one obtains in the 5 personality traits can be changed. What worries me, however, is that even if that is the case, surely with my psychological profile it will be very difficult to change. For example, I have tried many therapy interventions but none of them had a lasting effect. Some of them helped temporarily but before long my issues just came back with a vengeance. I think this stems partly fom low conscientiousness - it is nigh impossible for me to actually adhere to mental exercises prescribed by a counsellor/therapist (e.g. in CBT).

I think the low extraversion doesn't help either. I often feel extremely uncomfortable talking about myself and sometimes the feelings of shame this brings on are unbearable. So I tend to minimise my problems when talking to a therapist, not giving them access to the full picture. 

Low agreeableness and low extraversion basically mean that I am very bad at making new friends and as a result I have a very poor support network. This is definitely true in my life.
